conventions: TypeScript strict, ESM; Prettier 2 via @excalidraw/prettier-config (double quotes, trailing commas, 2-space indent, 80 cols); eslint-plugin-prettier enforces it, max-warnings 0.

Import order: package aliases (@excalidraw/common, @excalidraw/math, @excalidraw/element) first, then relative imports, then `import type` statements grouped last, blank line between groups (eslint import/order).
Inside packages/element/src import sibling modules relatively (./textRanges); outside packages/element import from "@excalidraw/element" and types from "@excalidraw/element/types".
AGENTS.md: never use the document/window globals in new code; use app.ownerDocument / app.ownerWindow, an element's ownerDocument, or svgRoot.ownerDocument.
AGENTS.md: combine object types with Merge<Base, Overrides> from "@excalidraw/common/utility-types", never Omit<...> & {...}.
Elements are immutable: change them only through mutateElement / scene.mutateElement / newElementWith, never by assignment.
A text element with no style ranges must not have the styleRanges key at all (not even undefined): add it with a conditional spread `...(ranges ? { styleRanges: ranges } : {})`.

decisions.topic: Two extra colour pickers next to the stroke picker

decisions.choice: Picking COLOR_PALETTE.transparent ("transparent") in either selection picker clears that attribute on the selection (patch value null); any other string sets it.

decisions.choice: A styled line is laid out with absolute run positions: lineWidth = sum of run widths measured with getLineWidth in the element's font; lineStart = 0 (left), (element.width - lineWidth) / 2 (center), element.width - lineWidth (right). LTR lines place runs left to right from lineStart; a line for which isRTL(line text) is true places runs in logical order from the right edge (first run ends at lineStart + lineWidth). Each run is drawn left-anchored at its x (canvas textAlign "left"; SVG tspan x with text-anchor "start").

A highlighted run gets a rect at (run.x, lineIndex * lineHeightPx), width run.width, height lineHeightPx, filled with applyDarkModeFilter(highlight, isDark); drawn before any text of that line (canvas fillRect; SVG <rect> appended to the element's <g> before that line's <text>).
decisions.reason: FR-18/FR-19: highlight sits behind the text and spans one line height.

decisions.choice: textEditorSelection defaults to null, so pretty-format adds the line `  "textEditorSelection": null,` right before each top-level `  "textToolHover": null,` line in regressionTests/history/contextmenu .snap files; that insertion is a deterministic perl tooling step per file, never vitest -u / yarn test:update.

decisions.choice: Both selection actions return captureUpdate CaptureUpdateAction.IMMEDIATELY when they change the element and CaptureUpdateAction.EVENTUALLY when they only pass app-state updates (popup open/close) or do nothing; the editor's input-time shift is not captured separately (the existing submit capture records it).

units.behaviour: Pure range model for styled text runs: normalize, apply a style, shift on edit, restore-validate, set on an element, and lay out styled runs per wrapped line for the canvas and SVG renderers.
rules: 1. Every function is pure: never mutate an input array or range object; return new arrays/objects (NFR-6).

2. normalizeStyleRanges(ranges, textLength): drop entries whose start/end are not finite integers, or with no non-empty color and no non-empty highlight; clamp start/end to [0, textLength]; drop empty or inverted spans; resolve overlaps by painting entries in input order onto a per-boundary segment list so a later entry overrides the attributes it sets (sweep over sorted unique boundaries, not per character); sort by start; merge touching neighbours (a.end === b.start) whose color and highlight are both equal; never emit an attribute key whose value is undefined. Returns a new array (possibly empty).

3. applyStyle(ranges, start, end, patch: { color?: string | null; highlight?: string | null }, textLength): if end <= start return the input array itself; otherwise split existing ranges at start and end, and for each sub-span in [start, end) set an attribute when the patch value is a string, delete it when null, keep it when the key is absent from the patch (a colour applied to highlighted text keeps the highlight); uncovered gaps inside [start, end) get only the patch's string attributes; then normalizeStyleRanges(result, textLength).

4. shiftRangesForEdit(ranges, oldText, newText): if the texts are equal return the input array. Find common prefix length p and common suffix length s, with s capped so p + s <= min(oldText.length, newText.length). The edit replaces old [p, oldEnd = oldText.length - s) with ins = newText.length - p - s inserted chars; delta = ins - (oldEnd - p). Map a range's start: <= p stays, >= oldEnd moves by delta, inside the deleted span collapses to p. Map its end: < p stays, >= oldEnd moves by delta, inside the deleted span collapses to p, and end === p stays p only when start < p and the range does not extend past oldEnd. Net effect: insertion strictly inside a range (start < p < end, or a replacement whose deleted span lies strictly inside) extends it by ins; insertion exactly at a range's start or end leaves it unstyled (Q2); deleted chars are removed from covering ranges; drop ranges that end up empty; normalizeStyleRanges against newText.length.

5. restoreStyleRanges(value: unknown, originalText: string): return undefined unless value is an array; keep entries that are non-null objects with finite integer start/end and color/highlight that are non-empty strings when present (copy only start, end, color, highlight); normalizeStyleRanges(kept, originalText.length); return undefined when the result is empty.
6. getStyleRanges(element): return element.styleRanges when it is a non-empty array, else an empty frozen array constant; hasStyleRanges(element) is getStyleRanges(element).length > 0.

7. withStyleRanges(element, ranges): normalize ranges against element.originalText.length; if the normalized list deep-equals getStyleRanges(element) return element; otherwise build `{ ...element }`, delete the styleRanges key, add it back only when the list is non-empty, then set version: element.version + 1, versionNonce: randomInteger(), updated: getUpdatedTimestamp() (both from @excalidraw/common).

8. splitRangesIntoLines(originalText, wrappedText, ranges): returns StyledTextLine[] with one entry per wrappedText line (split on 
 after normalizing 
). Align with two cursors: for each wrapped line, skip original characters that wrapping dropped (spaces or a single 
 at a break) until the next original char equals the line's first char, then map each line char to its original offset by advancing both cursors (a mismatch skips the original char); after a line, step over one original 
 if present. Group consecutive line chars whose original offsets fall in the same range (or none) into runs { text, color?, highlight? }; run texts concatenate exactly to the line; an empty line yields one run with text "". Never throw on misalignment: unmatched chars become unstyled. First normalize the input ranges against originalText.length, so stale out-of-bounds ranges are clamped.

9. getStyledTextLines(element, env?: RenderEnvironment): return null when !hasStyleRanges(element). Otherwise split element.text into lines with splitRangesIntoLines(element.originalText, element.text, styleRanges); for each line measure each run with getLineWidth(run.text, getFontString(element), env); lineWidth = sum; lineStart = 0 for left, (element.width - lineWidth) / 2 for center, element.width - lineWidth for right; if isRTL(line text) place runs right-to-left in logical order starting at lineStart + lineWidth, else left-to-right from lineStart. Each laid-out run is { text, color?, highlight?, x, width }.
10. Use getFontString and isRTL from @excalidraw/common, getLineWidth from ./textMeasurements, RenderEnvironment type from ./renderEnvironment; no DOM access.

rules: 1. Render <Excalidraw handleKeyboardGlobally={true} /> in beforeEach via render from "./test-utils"; use `const { h } = window;`, API from "./helpers/api", Keyboard/UI from "./helpers/ui", getTextEditor from "./queries/dom".

2. Open the editor on an existing text: API.setElements([text]); API.setSelectedElements([text]); Keyboard.keyPress(KEYS.ENTER); const editor = await getTextEditor(). Select with editor.setSelectionRange(start, end) followed by fireEvent.select(editor).
3. Apply styles with act(() => h.app.actionManager.executeAction(actionChangeTextRangeColor, "ui", { color })) (and the highlight action); actions are imported from "../actions".

4. For canvas assertions export with exportScene({ type: "canvas", data: { elements, files: {} } }) from "../scene/export" and spy with vi.spyOn on the 2d context prototype's fillText/fillRect, recording `this.fillStyle` at each call.
